stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Open, closed, locally closed immersions are representable and retain the corresponding scheme property after base change.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion,
resp.\ immersion),
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion), and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion).
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$.
conclusions: $f$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),

for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion,
resp.\ immersion),

for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),

there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion), and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion).

reason: Base-change stability of immersions gives the scheme-test implications; the proof invokes effective descent of separated locally quasi-finite morphisms along an étale chart to infer representability and the desired immersion property. Zariski locality finishes the equivalences.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Open, closed, locally closed immersions are representable and retain the corresponding scheme property after base change.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $Z \to Y \to X$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Z \to X$ is representable, locally of finite type, locally
quasi-finite, separated, and a monomorphism, then $Z \to Y$ is
representable, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite,
separated, and a monomorphism.
\item If $Z \to X$ is an immersion and $Y \to X$ is locally separated,
then $Z \to Y$ is an immersion.
\item If $Z \to X$ is a closed immersion and $Y \to X$ is separated,
then $Z \to Y$ is a closed immersion.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $Z \to Y \to X$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$Z \to Y$ is
representable, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite,
separated, and a monomorphism.

reason: The factorization Z→Y×_XZ→Y has first map a section and second a base change of Z→X. The section lemma and stability of the listed properties under base change and composition prove part (1); the proof states the same argument applies to the immersion and closed immersion cases.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Open, closed, locally closed immersions are representable and retain the corresponding scheme property after base change.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Then $|i| : |Z| \to |X|$ is a homeomorphism onto a
locally closed subset, and $i$ is a closed immersion if and only if
the image $|i|(|Z|) \subset |X|$ is a closed subset.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$|i| : |Z| \to |X|$ is a homeomorphism onto a
locally closed subset, and $i$ is a closed immersion if and only if
the image $|i|(|Z|) \subset |X|$ is a closed subset.

reason: The immersion is a homeomorphism onto a locally closed subset by the earlier topological embedding lemma. On a surjective étale scheme chart U→X its pullback is an immersion of schemes, which is closed exactly when its image is closed. This descends using the topological comparison and closed-immersion-local lemma.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \to X$ be an immersion of algebraic spaces over
$S$. Assume $Z \to X$ is quasi-compact.
There exists a factorization $Z \to \overline{Z} \to X$ where
$Z \to \overline{Z}$ is an open immersion and $\overline{Z} \to X$
is a closed immersion.
